name: tag_rename

path.udtDefinitionNamespace: only under an explicit _types_ allowlist entry
path.readable: the target must exist and its configuration must be readable, and its fingerprint is the item's Precondition token

newName.note: one path segment and nothing else: a /, ., [, ], *, ? or : anywhere in it is invalid_argument (details.items[].reason = newNameNotASingleSegment), because system.tag.rename takes a name and the target's own parent decides where the node lands

nativeOutcome: one system.tag.rename call per item, with the target's path, the new name and Abort as the collision policy; its single QualityCode is that item's outcome, and Observed state never decides success

preconditionToken.comparedRead: system.tag.exists(path), then system.tag.getConfiguration(path, false, false), then system.tag.exists(newPath) for every item, before any item executes
preconditionToken.raceWindow: D30 2: the compare and the change are two steps, so a competing writer can rewrite the target, remove it, or take its new path between the Preflight read and system.tag.rename. The handler narrows what it can (every target fingerprint and every free new path is read before any dispatch, a target the Preflight read found missing is refused with not_found, and an occupied new path is refused with conflict) and claims no atomicity. A new path that appears inside the window is refused by the Gateway's own Abort and reported as that item's conflict, so the race never costs a node; a target rewritten inside the window is renamed with content the caller never saw, and a caller that needs a narrower window re-reads with tag_get_config and retries the whole batch.

preflight: input, reserved provider and Target allowlist for every item before any item executes, with no rollback

runtimeTargetPolicy.allowlistMatch: the new path - the target's own parent plus items[].newName - as a provider-qualified config path prefix at segment boundaries; explicit * allows every provider but never a UDT definition
runtimeTargetPolicy.reservedProviderRefusal: permission_denied before Preflight for the target and for its new path, whatever the allowlist says, including an explicit *: a rename into the provider would place a node beside the policy document, and a rename of one of its nodes would move it (owner ruling 1)

targetPath.form: <provider>Tag, <provider>Folder or <provider>Folder/Tag, and <provider>_types_/... for a UDT definition
targetPath.noWildcard: a config target is one exact path: a *, ? or : anywhere in it is invalid_argument
targetPath.newPath: the path the Tool lands on is the target's own parent plus items[].newName, and it is that new path D30 6 measures, that must be free, and whose last segment is the new name

sourcePath.readable: system.tag.exists(path) must answer true (not_found, details.items[].reason = targetMissing) and system.tag.getConfiguration(path, false, false) must answer a node (upstream_error, reasons configurationReadFailed / configurationUnavailable) before any item executes
sourcePath.notAllowlistChecked: D30 6 checks the new path of a rename, not the old one: the target is bounded by the reserved-provider rule, its own readability and its fingerprint, and by the new path the caller names
sourcePath.reservedProvider: a target inside IgnitionMCPPolicy is refused with permission_denied (details.items[].reason = reservedProvider) before any read

udtDefinitionTargets: an explicit _types_ allowlist entry only, and the rule is positional: D30 6 names [provider]_types_/..., so only the first post-provider segment of the new path selects the definition namespace, and an entry has to name _types_ the same way. A bare * does not cover a UDT definition; a folder that merely happens to be called _types_ deeper in the path is an ordinary target (D30 6)
existingTargetFails: conflict (details.items[].reason = newPathExists): the new path already holds something, and D11 forbids replacing it
neverOverwrites: the handler sends collisionPolicy=Abort, so a new path that appears between the Preflight existence check and the dispatch is never overwritten: the call either raises or answers a non-Good QualityCode, and one bounded system.tag.exists check for that item's own new path decides it - a new path the Gateway answers as present is that item's conflict (details.items[].reason = newPathExists, the same reason the Preflight refusal uses) with the provider's own Native outcome still attached, and the target keeps its own name and parent either way
ambiguousOutcomeScope: an item whose own dispatch raised and whose new path the Gateway does not answer as present is outcome_unknown and ends the batch (later items are not_executed); a raised dispatch whose new path has appeared is that item's conflict, and an item whose dispatch answered an unattributable QualityCode is outcome_unknown, so the batch continues in both cases. Nothing is replayed

existenceCheck.call: system.tag.exists(path) and system.tag.exists(newPath) for every item, before any item executes
existenceCheck.why: a Gateway answers system.tag.getConfiguration for a path that is not there with a synthesized default node, so neither the target's presence nor the new path's absence can be read from a configuration read; the ticket #10 live run recorded the same synthesized node on 8.3.8 and 8.3.9
existenceCheck.targetMissing: not_found (details.items[].reason = targetMissing), and nothing is dispatched
existenceCheck.newPathPresent: conflict (details.items[].reason = newPathExists), and nothing is dispatched
existenceCheck.unanswered: upstream_error (reasons existenceCheckFailed / existenceCheckIndeterminate): a Gateway that raises or answers something that is not a boolean is never read as present or as absent
existenceCheck.observedReadBacks: the provider export is the independent presence check the harness uses for both paths

inputBounds.hardItemsPolicyRule: a deployment may raise the 20-target default through the Runtime Target Policy and never above the 100-target hard ceiling

observedState: two paths per item: the new path's own tag_get_config read, `system.tag.getConfiguration(newPath, false, false)`, published with the D30 2 fingerprint of that read, and the old path's absence, read back with `system.tag.exists(path)`. Both are Observed state and never decide success, and the new path's fingerprint is the token the caller's next tag_update/tag_delete would use
deniedMutationAudit: after a usable Policy is read, a refused Target and a refused Precondition each produce one `decision` row and no dispatch; `off` records nothing, and `required` refuses the call when the denial row cannot be written
outcomePreservation: a dispatched batch reports its per-item Native outcomes whatever the Observed-state budget or the serializer does; an Observed configuration that cannot be returned is an explicit `limit_exceeded` observed error, and the result is re-rendered without the Observed state rather than replacing the outcomes
